name: Cost Baseline
purpose: A time-phased budget used to measure, monitor and control cost performance. It is built by summing project costs per time period into a cumulative cost curve (the S-curve) against which actual cost, planned cost and funds spent are tracked. It is developed once and is not expected to change unless the scope changes significantly.

tailoring: The baseline generally includes contingency reserve for known risks and generally does not include management reserve; management reserve is held above the baseline but is part of the project budget. Company policy may differ.
The baseline may be shown to display funding constraints, funding requirements or different funding sources.
The organization may not require a graphic; a spreadsheet or an internal budgeting system display may be used instead.

notes: The book gives no Document Element table for this form, so elements is empty. The prose says to record the cost baseline as the cumulative cost curve but does not give a method for spreading cost over periods or for sizing the reserves; those are not stated in the book here.
